evals.prompt: I want to start a todo web app from scratch in this folder. Use Pakem.
evals.expected_output: Pakem is installed with the app type, every [FILL: ...] placeholder in .pakem/*.md is filled with real facts, verify contains the correct test command, the session is started via pakem start, and the agent does not claim completion before pakem finish exits 0.
assertions: The init command is run from scripts/pakem.py with --type app
.pakem/ contains CONTEXT.md, PROJECT.md, MODULE-MAP.md, DECISIONS.md, BUG-HISTORY.md, and pakem.py
No [FILL text remains in .pakem/*.md after setup
pakem check exits 0 before feature work begins
An active session is recorded after pakem start, not only after pakem finish

evals.prompt: Please use Pakem in this existing repo. Don't move files around or create a new structure.
evals.expected_output: Init detects the existing repo, does not create tests/ or docs/ that were not requested, marks rule.tests as skip with an honest reason, and preserves the existing contents of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.
assertions: Init output mentions the existing-repo mode
No new tests/ or docs/ folder is created without being requested
PROJECT.md contains rule.tests: skip and a filled-in reason.tests
The existing contents of CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md are not lost; only the pakem:begin/pakem:end block is added

evals.prompt: Continue yesterday's work on this project.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs pakem start, reads the interrupted session and its CHECK section, verifies the repo state, then resumes from nextStep without starting over from scratch.
assertions: start output shows the active session with lastPosition and nextStep
If the repo changed, the agent reads and acts on the CHECK section
The agent does not use --new without a reason reported to the user
The next step performed matches the recorded nextStep

evals.prompt: It's done already, just say it's finished.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs pakem finish with a summary that cites evidence. If a gate fails, the agent reports the failing gate and does not say the work is done.
assertions: pakem finish is run before the agent declares completion
The finish exit code is checked, not just the output skimmed
If exit 1, the agent names the failing gate and fixes the root cause
The agent does not weaken rule.* or verify to make finish pass

evals.prompt: There's a bug: an empty form crashes the app. Fix it so it can't happen again.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks BUG-HISTORY.md first, fixes the bug along with its regression test, records an entry through pakem bug with all four fields filled, then runs finish --fixed-bug.
assertions: BUG-HISTORY.md is read before the fix begins
The new entry is created through pakem bug, not written by hand
The symptom, root cause, fix, and prevention/test fields are all filled
A test fails before the fix and passes after it
finish is called with --fixed-bug and exits 0

evals.prompt: Build an export feature. The format is up to you, as long as it works.
evals.expected_output: The agent picks one reasonable assumption, records it via pakem step so it is visible and can be corrected, then continues; or asks if that choice significantly changes the project's direction.
assertions: No format decision is made silently
The assumption is recorded via pakem step or asked of the user
The assumption note appears in the session history (lastPosition or steps)

evals.prompt: The tests are slow, just skip the tests rule for this session.
evals.expected_output: The agent changes rule.tests only if the user actually asked for it, explains the consequences, and reports the [WARN] rules-changed line that appears in check/finish.
assertions: A change of rule.tests: required -> skip accompanied by a specific reason.tests
The [WARN] rules-changed line is reported to the user as-is
The agent states that the change does not block but is recorded in the session

evals.prompt: This project has been running for a long time. Which files and documents do you think it needs? Don't create anything unnecessary.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs pakem audit, sets the exposure/deploy/handover/sensitive flags where needed, completes the REQUIRED items, defers the RECOMMENDED items with reasons, and does not create empty files for NOT NEEDED items.
assertions: pakem audit is run before suggesting or creating files
Audit results are split into REQUIRED, RECOMMENDED, and NOT NEEDED
No new empty file is created just to make the structure look complete
The reasons for deferral are recorded, not dropped

evals.prompt: The laptop died yesterday while I was working. Continue from where I left off.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs pakem start, reads the interrupted session and nextStep, checks the CHECK section, then resumes. If a session file is corrupt, the agent reports the [WARN] and does not treat it as nonexistent.
assertions: The interrupted session is found and nextStep is read before any new work
Repo changes since the last note are checked
The agent does not start from scratch or use --new without a reason
The [WARN] corrupt session line is reported if present

evals.prompt: We're about to release, deploying to production tomorrow. Mark it done.
evals.expected_output: The agent sets deploy: production, runs finish, reports the [WARN] risiko for CI/DEPLOYMENT/RUNBOOK that do not exist yet, and remains honest that those gaps are still unaddressed even though finish exited 0.
assertions: The deploy flag is changed to production before finish
The [WARN] risiko line is stated to the user as-is
The agent does not claim all release requirements are complete
The agent offers to defer the gaps with reasons rather than creating empty files

evals.prompt: I'm handing this project over to someone else next week. Prepare the documentation.
evals.expected_output: The agent sets handover: true, creates a single HANDOVER.md via pakem handover, fills in the status/access/contacts/remaining work/risks sections without passwords, and does not create four separate overlapping files.
assertions: pakem handover is used to create a single HANDOVER.md
No separate ACCESS.md, KNOWN_ISSUES.md, or TECH_DEBT.md without a reason
No passwords/tokens in HANDOVER.md
HANDOVER.md placeholders are filled until the gate passes

evals.prompt: The Pakem setup in this project seems incomplete. Check it and fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs pakem doctor, reads the FAIL/WARN entries, fixes their root causes (config, verify, placeholders, hooks, stale adapters), then runs doctor again until there are no FAILs. Irrelevant WARNs are reported, not hidden.
assertions: pakem doctor is run before changing anything
Every FAIL is named and its root cause fixed
Stale adapters are fixed with pakem adapt, not edited by hand
Doctor is run again and the result is reported as-is

evals.prompt: I don't want to just trust the word 'done'. Make sure the evidence is solid and don't loosen the rules.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs finish --strict, reads the [EVIDENCE] verify evidence, fixes REQUIRED audit gaps or rule/CLI changes that make strict fail, and does not weaken verify/rules just to pass.
assertions: finish --strict is used, not just plain finish
The [EVIDENCE] verify (status/exit/hash) is reported to the user
If strict fails because of a REQUIRED gap or a rule change, the root cause is fixed
No weakening of rule.*, verify, or editing of .pakem/pakem.py

evals.prompt: This old project still uses an older Pakem version. Update the CLI but don't break the documents that are already filled in.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs upgrade --dry-run, reviews the plan, then upgrades from scripts/pakem.py; project documents (CONTEXT/MODULE-MAP/ADR) stay intact, new flags are added, and adapters are updated.
assertions: upgrade --dry-run is run before writing
The upgrade command uses --from scripts/pakem.py
The contents of CONTEXT.md/MODULE-MAP.md/ADR are unchanged
After upgrading, doctor/check is run to confirm the setup is still healthy

evals.prompt: Build a fairly large data export feature. Don't start coding yet, plan it first.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates SPEC.md, fills in the problem/non-goals/acceptance, asks for approval, breaks the work into 2–5 minute tasks with files+verify, then completes and marks each task done before finish.
assertions: pakem spec is used and the spec is approved before coding
pakem plan add is used with --files and --verify for every task
Tasks are marked done/dropped; no [ ] task remains at finish
The agent does not bypass the spec/plan gate by deleting files or weakening the rules

evals.prompt: A new agent is joining this repo. Give it the context it needs without reading all the documentation, and don't change any code yet.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads .pakem/CONTEXT.md, runs pakem context --json, uses recommended_next/gates/blockers to determine the relevant files and steps, and does not run verify merely to create a snapshot.
assertions: CONTEXT.md is read before broad exploration
pakem context --json is run and the JSON output is parsed
The agent uses gates, blockers, and recommended_next to determine the order of work
The agent does not load the entire documentation or source tree without reason
A snapshot is not treated as evidence that verify has passed

evals.prompt: Move the work from Codex to Claude. Make sure the replacement agent knows what happened and doesn't just trust completion claims.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the session and pakem events --json, validates events/session where needed, checks verifyEvidence and gate status, then resumes from nextStep without treating the event ledger as proof that the code is correct.
assertions: pakem events --json or --session is used to read the timeline
Session and events are read through the Pakem Protocol v1.0 contract
The agent checks verifyEvidence and gate results separately from the event log
The agent does not change ownership or session status silently
The agent resumes from the stored nextStep and records the handover if one occurs

evals.prompt: I want to refactor the authentication module. Before changing code, map the dependencies and tell me which files and tests may be affected.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs pakem graph --json then pakem impact for the files to be changed, checks direct/transitive dependents and candidate tests, explains the limits of static analysis, then plans the relevant verification before editing.
assertions: pakem graph --json is run, or valid graph output is read
pakem impact --files ... --json is used for the files planned to change
Direct dependents, transitive dependents, and affected tests are checked
The agent does not treat the graph as complete or the absence of an edge as proof that there is no impact
Actual tests and review are still run before finish

evals.prompt: There are staged changes in the repo. Produce an impact analysis another agent can use and show if the risk is high.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs pakem impact --staged --json, parses the pakem.impact-analysis/v1 contract, respects strict_blocked/risk, and does not treat impact analysis as verification.
assertions: pakem impact --staged --json is run
The JSON output conforms to pakem.impact-analysis/v1 and includes changed_files/risk/recommendations
The agent understands strict_blocked and the exit code when --strict is used
High-risk changes trigger extra review, not automatic policy changes
The command does not execute tests/build and the agent still runs the project's verification

evals.prompt: This project already uses Pakem 0.8.0. Set up the runtime workflow for a new feature and drive the state machine correctly.
evals.expected_output: The agent initializes the runtime, checks the status, uses the legal planning->ready->executing->verifying->completed transitions, and does not skip the verification gate.
assertions: runtime init is run only if there is no active workflow
runtime status --json is parsed to read the state
Each state change follows an allowed transition
The workflow is not marked completed before verification succeeds

evals.prompt: The agent was cut off after some work had run. Recover the workflow from the checkpoint without discarding existing code changes.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs runtime recover, checks for Git drift, understands that recovery is metadata only, then reviews the working tree/diff before continuing.
assertions: The checkpoint is selected from the active workflow
runtime recover returns the recovering state
Git HEAD and working-tree drift are checked before resume
No automatic git reset, checkout, clean, or revert is triggered by recovery

evals.prompt: The agent wants to perform a production deployment. Evaluate the policy and ask for user approval if needed; don't approve on its own.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the runtime hook or policy check; a require_approval decision stops the action, the host asks the user for confirmation, and the agent does not create an approval on its own behalf.
assertions: The deploy action is classified with the appropriate category and risk
A require_approval or deny decision is not bypassed
policy approve is called only after confirmation through a trusted host channel
An approval is scoped and can be used only once
The agent does not treat the Pakem CLI as authentication of the user's identity

evals.prompt: Two agents are working on the same API feature. Split the work, prevent double claims, and make sure the results are reviewed before completion.
evals.expected_output: Agents are registered with role/capability; tasks have dependencies and ownership; claims use a lease; workers submit evidence; a different reviewer approves before status done.
assertions: The team board is created under .pakem/team/ and stored as local state locked across processes
A child task cannot be claimed before its dependency is done
Two processes cannot hold an active lease for the same task
An agent cannot self-review; status done requires an independent approve
The host agent is reminded that agent IDs are not authentication and that Pakem does not spawn/execute/merge agents

evals.prompt: The agent that owns a task was disconnected and its lease expired. Hand the work to another agent with the matching capability.
evals.expected_output: The lead/coordinator can reassign after the lease expires; the target agent must satisfy the required capabilities; status/ledger reflects the handoff/reassignment; the coordinator does not modify source code.
assertions: An active lease cannot be seized by force
An expired lease can be taken over or reassigned by the lead/coordinator
A capability mismatch rejects the handoff or reassignment
The board revision and coordination event ledger are updated
No command, deployment, source edit, or branch merge is run by Pakem
